old_membership_record.rationale:
The January 22, 2026 choice is Norman Part B amendment No. 2 to H.R.7148, not passage of the appropriations package or a vote on one recipient. It inserts “except Community Project Funding/Congressionally Directed Spending as specified in Division B” after “Act” on page3line1, in the first sentence of the matter-preceding-Division-A section4 explanatory-statement clause. That sentence otherwise gives the named explanatory statement the same effect for allocation of funds and implementation of divisionsAthroughD as a joint explanatory statement of a conference committee. The proposed exception concerns that incorporation-effect rule. It is not itself a separate sentence cancelling every named appropriation, and the candidate does not turn debate shorthand about earmarks into a different operative prohibition.

H.Res.1014 first deemed the report's Part A changes adopted. Those add separate statement-effect paragraphs for the7006and7147material and other specified changes; this amendment's page3operator is not silently moved into those later paragraphs. The rule's later engrossment instructions add/relabel other divisions and permit specified corrections. The later assembled EH or Senate amendment is not substituted for the own January22amending stage. The source's actual introduction line says January20,2026; the older retained source metadata instead labels the IHprimary January22. This metadata discrepancy is retained historically; the candidate uses the primary's printed January20introduction and January22amending stage. No intent behind the older label is inferred. The printed division lists/cross-references are not silently repaired.

The qualified Immigration relationship follows a stated project purpose, not a recipient's name or an assumed programme beneficiary. The Record's DivisionBCommunityProjectFunding/CongressionallyDirectedSpending table, printedH1615/physicalPDF263, lists HHSAdministrationforChildrenandFamilies and “City of Whitewater, WI, to reduce poverty through an immigrant liaison,” with85000dollars in the Amount($)column. That purpose expressly relates to immigrant-facing liaison work. It does not establish any person's citizenship, lawful presence, eligibility, actual service use or immigration result. Names of other cultural, educational, Tribal, international, health or social-service recipients alone do not establish their personal Immigration rules.

Seven direct DivisionBappropriation branches remain a separate part of the same material chain. They direct funds to specified projects/amounts in the named table, with their own accounts, qualifications and exceptions. In particular, the ChildrenandFamiliesServicesPrograms heading says40801000dollars shall be used for the projects and amounts in that table, and retains its express241PHSAct/205exceptions. This proposed amendment does not literally strike that command or its references. The other direct workforce,HRSA,SAMHSA,community-living and two education branches also retain their printed instructions and exceptions. Their existence prevents this candidate from asserting that changing section4alone necessarily eliminates the Whitewater allocation, rescinds1386898000dollars or removes every listed project. The precise interaction, enforceability and fiscal implementation remain legal/application questions; no binding appropriation outcome is invented.

Names of other cultural, educational, Tribal, international, health or social-service recipients alone do not establish their personal Immigration rules.

R. 7148 Making further consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, and for other purposes. _______________________________________________________________________ IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES January 20, 2026 Mr. Cole introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Appropriations, and in addition to the Committees on the Budget, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned _______________________________________________________________________ A BILL Making further consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, and for other purposes. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled, SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE. This Act may be cited as the ``Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026''. SEC. 2. TABLE OF CONTENTS. Sec. 1. Short title. Sec. 2. Table of contents. Sec. 3. References. Sec. 4. Explanatory statement. Sec. 5. Statement of appropriations. REFERENCES. Except as expressly provided otherwise, any reference to ``this Act'' contained in any division of this Act shall be treated as referring only to the provisions of that division. SEC. 4. The explanatory statement regarding this Act, printed in the House section of the Congressional Record on or about January 21, 2026, and submitted by the chair of the Committee on Appropriations of the House, shall have the same effect with respect to the allocation of funds and implementation of divisions A through D of this Act as if it were a joint explanatory statement of a committee of conference.
